# Scene API

<!-- Generated by schema_markdown() in components/wisp_scene/src/schema.cpp; do not edit.
     schema_test's DocIsUpToDate fails when this file is stale and writes the new text to
     build/sim/scene-api.md. -->

A scene's `main.lua` returns its widget tree, built with the constructors in the global
`ui` table (scene-runtime-core spec 4). String keys are properties, array entries are
children:

```lua
local count = state(0)
local d = wisp.device.info()
local s = d.safe_area
return ui.screen { align = "center", justify = "center",
  -- {top, right, bottom, left}: keeps the column inside the safe area
  pad = { s.y1, d.width - 1 - s.x2, d.height - 1 - s.y2, s.x1 },
  ui.column { gap = 12, align = "center",
    ui.label { text = bind(count, function(v) return "clicked " .. v end) },
    ui.button { text = "+1", on_click = function() count:set(count:get() + 1) end },
  },
}
```

Rules:

- The root must be `ui.screen`. It fills the whole display and has no padding of its
  own: the scene lays itself out (see Screen shape below).
- At most 2000 widgets per tree, counting the rows every list has built: rows
  past it are not built, and the scene's log says so. A string value is at
  most 64 KB.
- One update (the tree, or what one handler changes) is at most 1 MB, counting
  64 bytes per widget, property and change plus every string value: a large
  string shown by many widgets counts once per widget ("ui update too large").
- A widget can be the child of only one other widget; `ui.screen` only the root.
- Unknown widgets and properties and values of the wrong type are errors at the line
  that built the widget.
- A *bindable* property also takes a `state`, `computed` or `bind`; the widget follows
  its value. Every value it takes is checked like a plain one, at the line that built
  the widget.
- `"fill"` across a `column` or `row` (a column child's `w`, a row child's `h`) is
  the parent's whole size, so inside a parent that is itself sized by its content
  (the default) it can come out 0: give that parent a size or `"fill"` too.
- `scene.on_show()` first runs right after `main.lua` returns, before the tree is on
  the screen; what it changes is still applied after the tree is built.

## Value types

| Type | Values |
|---|---|
| size | integer pixels, `"fill"` or `"content"` |
| integer | an integer (`120.0` counts as one) |
| number | an integer or a float |
| string | a string or a number |
| boolean | `true` or `false` |
| color | `"#RRGGBB"` or a theme token: `accent`, `text`, `muted`, `surface`, `bg`, `danger`, `ok`, `warn` |
| font | `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`, or integer pixels 16 to 128 (see Font sizes) |
| align | `start`, `center`, `end` |
| justify | `start`, `center`, `end`, `between`, `around`, `evenly` |
| pad | integer pixels on every side, or `{top, right, bottom, left}` (CSS order), each 0 to 512 |
| enum | one of the listed words |
| function | a function |
| items | a table (an array), or a state holding one |
| series | up to 4 tables of up to 128 numbers each |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Bindable | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `w` | size | yes | 0 to 4096 pixels, "fill" or "content" |
| `h` | size | yes | 0 to 4096 pixels, "fill" or "content" |
| `grow` | integer | yes | integer 0 to 255 |
| `pad` | pad | yes | 0 to 512 pixels or {top, right, bottom, left} of 0 to 512 each |
| `gap` | integer | yes | integer 0 to 512 |
| `align` | align | yes | one of start, center, end |
| `justify` | justify | yes | one of start, center, end, between, around, evenly |
| `bg` | color | yes | "#RRGGBB" or one of accent, text, muted, surface, bg, danger, ok, warn |
| `fg` | color | yes | "#RRGGBB" or one of accent, text, muted, surface, bg, danger, ok, warn |
| `radius` | integer | yes | integer 0 to 4096 |
| `border` | integer | yes | integer 0 to 64 |
| `font` | font | yes | one of xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl, or an integer 16 to 128 (pixels) |
| `hidden` | boolean | yes | boolean |
| `opa` | number | yes | number from 0 to 1 |
| `ref` | string | no | a name of 1 to 64 bytes |

| `name` | enum | yes | `home`, `settings`, `wifi`, `battery`, `bell`, `play`, `pause`, `stop`, `prev`, `next`, `plus`, `minus`, `ok`, `close`, `trash`, `edit`, `refresh`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`, `upload`, `download`, `save`, `list`, `image`, `audio`, `warning`, `volume`, `mute`, `envelope`, `eye`, `eye_slash`, `bluetooth`, `gps`, `power`, `bolt`, `phone`, `file`, `folder`, `keyboard`, `shuffle`, `loop`, `copy`, `cut`, `paste`, `drop`, `microphone`, `microphone_slash`, `headphones`, `comment`, `comments`, `robot`, `brain`, `magic`, `lightbulb`, `clock`, `stopwatch`, `hourglass`, `calendar`, `history`, `sun`, `moon`, `cloud`, `cloud_sun`, `cloud_moon`, `cloud_rain`, `snowflake`, `wind`, `thermometer`, `umbrella`, `fire`, `tasks`, `check_circle`, `check_square`, `square`, `sticky_note`, `book`, `bookmark`, `flag`, `newspaper`, `info`, `question`, `exclamation`, `times_circle`, `lock`, `unlock`, `user`, `heart`, `star`, `smile`, `frown`, `thumbs_up`, `trophy`, `gift`, `search`, `globe`, `map_marker`, `link`, `share`, `camera`, `gamepad`, `sliders`, `filter`, `calculator`, `coffee`, `utensils`, `shopping_cart`, `car`, `bed`, `running`, `undo`, `redo` |
| `src` | string | no | a path assets/&lt;name>.png, .jpg or .jpeg |
| `value` | number | yes | number |
| `min` | number | yes | number |
| `max` | number | yes | number |
| `checked` | boolean | yes | boolean |
| `cols` | integer | no | integer 1 to 16 |
| `direction` | enum | no | `v`, `h` |
| `type` | enum | no | `line`, `bar` |
| `series` | series | yes | a table of up to 4 tables of up to 128 numbers |
| `items` | items | yes | a table |
| `row` | function | no | function |
| `row_h` | integer | yes | integer 1 to 4096 |
| `draw` | function | no | function |
| `width` | integer | yes | integer 0 to 512 |
| `wrap` | boolean | yes | boolean |
| `on_click` | function | no | function |
| `on_long_press` | function | no | function |
| `on_change` | function | no | function |

`on_click` and `on_long_press` take no arguments; `on_change(value)` gets the new text,
value or checked state. `row(item, index)` returns the widget for one list row and is
only called for visible rows. `draw(g)` draws a canvas.

## Font sizes

`font` is a token or a size in pixels from 16 to 128. `xs`, `sm` and `md` are the
16-pixel body font, `lg` is 24, `xl` 32 and `xxl` 48. Sizes 16 to 19 are the body
font too; from 20 on the text is drawn from a vector font in steps of 20, 24, 28, 32,
40, 48, 64, 80, 96 and 128 pixels, and a size between two steps gets the lower one
(50 is 48). Symbols (`ui.icon`) come in 16, 24, 32 and 48 pixels, again the largest
that is not above the size.

Large sizes suit short text such as a number or a time. Each glyph is drawn the
first time it is shown at a size, which takes a few milliseconds at the largest
sizes, and only a few glyphs per size are kept (13 at 128 pixels), so a long text in
a large size is redrawn slowly.

## Widgets

Every widget takes the common properties: `w`, `h`, `grow`, `pad`, `bg`, `fg`, `radius`, `border`, `font`, `hidden`, `opa`, `ref`, `on_click`, `on_long_press`.

| Widget | Children | Properties besides the common ones |
|---|---|---|
| `ui.screen` | yes | `gap`, `align`, `justify` |
| `ui.column` | yes | `gap`, `align`, `justify` |
| `ui.row` | yes | `gap`, `align`, `justify` |
| `ui.stack` | yes | `gap`, `align`, `justify` |
| `ui.grid` | yes | `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `cols` |
| `ui.spacer` | no | - |
| `ui.scroll` | yes | `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `direction` |
| `ui.label` | no | `text`, `wrap` |
| `ui.icon` | no | `name` |
| `ui.image` | no | `src` |
| `ui.button` | yes | `text` |
| `ui.checkbox` | no | `text`, `checked`, `on_change` |
| `ui.switch` | no | `checked`, `on_change` |
| `ui.slider` | no | `value`, `min`, `max`, `on_change` |
| `ui.input` | no | `text`, `placeholder`, `password`, `max_len`, `on_change` |
| `ui.bar` | no | `value`, `min`, `max` |
| `ui.arc` | no | `value`, `min`, `max`, `width` |
| `ui.chart` | no | `type`, `series`, `min`, `max` |
| `ui.list` | no | `items`, `row` (required), `row_h` |
| `ui.canvas` | no | `draw` |

### list, canvas, chart, image, icon

- `ui.list`: only the rows around the visible part exist. `row(item, index)` runs for
  each row as it scrolls into view and its widgets are dropped when it scrolls away;
  bindings inside a row live as long as the row. Every row is `row_h` pixels tall (default
  48) and as wide as the list, whatever its own `w` and `h`. A row cannot use `ref` or
  hold another `ui.list`. Setting `items` builds the visible rows again.
- `ui.canvas`: `draw(g)` runs once the canvas is built and again whenever a state it
  read changes. `g` only works while `draw` runs, for at most 512 calls:
  `g:fill(color)`, `g:line(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts)`, `g:circle(cx, cy, r, opts)`,
  `g:arc(cx, cy, r, start, end, opts)` (degrees, clockwise from 3 o'clock),
  `g:rect(x, y, w, h, opts)`, `g:text(x, y, text, opts)`. `opts` is optional:
  `color` (a colour, default `text`), `width` (lines and outlines, 0 to 512, default
  1), `radius` (rect corners, 0 to 4096), `fill` (boolean: circle and rect filled),
  `font` (text: a token or 16 to 128 pixels, as for the property). A canvas is `fill`
  in both directions unless given a size. A canvas of more than 524,288 pixels stays
  empty ("ui.canvas: too large" in the scene's log). The `g:text` that takes the
  update past 1 MB is the error "ui update too large".
- `ui.chart`: `series` is up to 4 tables of up to 128 numbers, drawn in `accent`, `ok`,
  `warn` and `danger`, between `min` and `max` (default 0 and 100); `type` is `line`
  (default) or `bar`.
- `ui.image`: `src` is a PNG or a baseline (not progressive) JPEG in the scene's
  `assets/`, at most 1024 pixels a side and 524,288 pixels in all. A file that is
  missing, cannot be decoded or is too large leaves the image empty and is reported in
  the scene's log. The decoded images and canvases of a scene take at most 4 MB
  together; the one that would pass it stays empty ("too large").
- `ui.icon`: the symbol `name` in the current `font`.

## Screen shape

The screen may be a rectangle, a rounded rectangle or a circle, and a scene gets all of
it: `ui.screen` fills the display, and pixels outside the visible shape are simply not
shown. Lay out from what the device reports instead of fixed margins:

- `wisp.device.info()` has `width`, `height`, `shape` (`rect`, `rounded_rect` or
  `circle`), `corner_radius` (the rounded rectangle's radius, half the smaller side for
  a circle, 0 for a rectangle) and `safe_area` (`x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, inclusive: the
  largest centred rectangle that is visible everywhere, with a small margin).
- `wisp.device.info().status_area` (`x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, inclusive) is the system's
  status capsule at the top centre of the safe area. It is given whether or not the
  capsule shows, so a scene that keeps clear of it never has its layout jump.
- `wisp.device.row_span(y)` returns `x1, x2`, the first and last visible pixel of
  screen row `y`, or `nil` when the row shows nothing or is off the screen.

A centred block can pad the screen by the safe area, as in the example above. Content
near the top or bottom edge can be inset by `row_span` at its own rows and use the
width the safe area would waste. Scrolling content may pass through the invisible
corners, but when scrolled to either end its first and last item must be whole on the
visible screen: pad the list (per side) so that `row_span` at the item's top and
bottom rows covers its left and right edges.

A swipe to the right that starts within 16 pixels of the left edge of the
visible screen (rows within the safe area's height) is the system's back
gesture, at any angle: a touch there reaches the scene like any other, and
only once it has moved 24 pixels to the right -- however far up or down --
does the system take it, and the widget under it then gets no click.
Dragging back to the left of that distance before release cancels it and
nothing happens. A touch on the on-screen keyboard never starts it.

A swipe down that starts within 16 pixels of the top of the visible screen
(measured from the first visible pixel of the column it starts in) is the
system's pull-down gesture, at any angle: the touch reaches the scene like
any other until it has moved 24 pixels down, when the system opens its
pull-down panel and the widget under the finger gets no click
(`PRESS_LOST`). It never starts while the keyboard, the error panel or a
confirmation dialog is up. A tap on the status capsule (at `status_area`, shown while scenes run
in the background or notifications are unread) opens the panel too.

## Helpers

- `ui.show_if(s, widget)` returns `widget`, shown while `s` (a state, computed, bind or
  boolean) is truthy and hidden otherwise. The widget is never rebuilt.
- `ui.ref(name)` returns a handle to the widget with `ref = name` in the current tree,
  looked up when a method is called:
  - `h:value()`: the current text of an `input`, value of a `slider`, or checked state of
    a `checkbox` or `switch`.
  - `h:scroll_to(i)`: scrolls a `list` or `scroll` to its `i`-th item (from 1).
  - `h:focus()`: focuses an `input` and opens the on-screen keyboard.

## wisp.store

A scene's own persistent data (scene-runtime-core spec 5.4): a key/value space plus up
to 16 named collections of JSON records, kept under the scene's `data/` and never seen
by any other scene.

- `wisp.store.get(key)` returns the stored value, or `nil` if `key` has none.
- `wisp.store.set(key, value)` returns `true`, or `nil` and a code; `value == nil`
  deletes `key`.
- `wisp.store.batch(fn)` calls `fn` with every `wisp.store` write inside it held back
  until `fn` returns: if `fn` raises, or any one of those writes would itself fail,
  none of them take effect and the call returns `nil, "batch_aborted"`; otherwise
  they all do and the call returns `true`. Batches may nest.
- `wisp.store.collection(name)` returns a handle `c` for one of up to 16 collections
  (`name` is 1 to 32 bytes of lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`; `"kv"` is
  reserved for the key/value space above):
  - `c:insert(record)` returns the new record's `id` (an integer), or `nil` and a code.
  - `c:update(id, record)` returns `true`, or `nil` and a code.
  - `c:delete(id)` returns `true`, or `nil` and a code (`"not_found"` for an `id` that
    does not exist).
  - `c:find(filter?, opts?)` returns a list of matching records, each with its `id`
    field set.

`record` is a table with string keys. `id` in it is reserved: `insert` and `update`
strip it out before storing (so a record `find` returns can be passed straight back to
`update`), and it is always the id the store itself hands out, never a stored field.
`filter` (a table) keeps only records equal on every field it gives; `filter.id` tests
the record id rather than a stored field. `opts.sort` orders by one top-level field
(numbers by value, strings by bytes; a record missing it sorts last whatever
`opts.desc` says); `sort = "id"`, or no `sort` at all, means id order, which is
insertion order -- newest first once `opts.desc` is set. `opts.limit` and
`opts.offset` page the result.

Codes: `quota_exceeded`, `record_too_large`, `too_many_collections`,
`not_serializable`, `too_deep`, `not_found`, `ids_exhausted`, `batch_aborted`. A key,
collection name or record of the wrong type, length or shape is a Lua error instead,
at the line that made the call.

## Lua environment

Scenes run Lua 5.5 in a sandbox of their own. Only the `string`, `table`, `math`,
`utf8` and `coroutine` libraries and the safe base functions are there (no `io`,
`os`, `require`, `dofile` or `loadfile`; `load` takes text only). Every file is
compiled so that a global name it does not declare is a compile error: use `local`
for your own names. The globals a scene may use are `ui`, `state`, `computed`,
`bind`, `wisp`, `scene` and the standard ones above.

- Each message (the entry file, a handler, a timer, a callback) may run for 200 ms,
  and a scene's Lua memory is at most 2 MB; past either the scene stops with an error.
- `print(...)` writes one line to the scene's log, like `wisp.log.info`.
- `wisp.import("lib/<name>")` runs `lib/<name>.lua` from the scene's package once
  and returns what it returned (`true` for nothing); later imports of the same
  path return the same value. An import cycle is an error.
- `state(v)`: a value the UI can follow. `s:get()` reads it, `s:set(v)` writes it;
  every bound property and computed that read it is brought up to date after the
  current message. Writing an equal value (by value for numbers, strings and
  booleans, by reference for tables) changes nothing.
- `computed(fn)`: `c:get()` is `fn()`, worked out again only after something it read
  changed. `fn` may not call `:set()`.
- `bind(s, fn)`: a computed whose value is `fn(s:get())`; `s` is a state, computed
  or bind. Pass any of the three as a bindable property.

## wisp.timer

- `wisp.timer.after(ms, fn)` runs `fn()` once, `ms` milliseconds from now;
  `wisp.timer.every(ms, fn)` every `ms` milliseconds. Both return a handle, or `nil`
  and `interval_too_small` (below 50 ms) or `too_many_timers` (32 set at once).
- `h:cancel()` stops it and returns whether it had still to run.
- Each run is a message of its own. Timers keep running in the background and
  while the screen is off; they end when the scene closes.

## wisp.device

- `wisp.device.info()` returns `width`, `height`, `shape`, `corner_radius`,
  `safe_area` and `status_area` (see Screen shape), `lang` (`"zh"`, `"ja"` or
  `"en"`), `utc_offset` (minutes east of UTC), `time` (seconds since the epoch,
  `nil` until the clock is set), `battery` (percent, `nil` when unknown),
  `charging` and `wifi` (`"off"`, `"connecting"`, `"backoff"` or
  `"connected"`).
- `wisp.device.row_span(y)`: see Screen shape.
- `wisp.device.on(event, fn)` calls `fn(info)`, with `info` as `info()` returns
  it, on each `"battery"` change, each `"minute"` of the clock and each
  `"lang"` change. Any other event name is an error.

## wisp.log

- `wisp.log.info(...)`, `wisp.log.warn(...)` and `wisp.log.error(...)` write one
  line of their arguments, joined with tabs like `print`, to the scene's log
  (tag `scene.<id>`, at most 512 bytes a line), which the admin page and the agent
  can read. It is kept in memory only.

## wisp.http

```lua
wisp.http.get("https://api.example.com/now", nil, function(err, res)
  if err then return end
  print(res.status, res.json and res.json.temp)
end)
wisp.http.post(url, { a = 1 }, { headers = { authorization = "Bearer x" } }, cb)
```

- `wisp.http.get(url, opts, cb)` and `wisp.http.post(url, body, opts, cb)`: `opts`
  (may be `nil` or left out) is `{headers = {name = value}}`; a `body` table is sent
  as JSON (with `Content-Type: application/json` unless a header names one), a
  string as it is.
- `cb(err, res)` runs later as a message of its own: `res` is `{status, headers,
  body, json}`, `headers` with lowercase names, `json` the decoded body when the
  content type mentions JSON and it parses; `err` is `nil` on success.
- Only `https://` URLs (`not_https`) to a host listed in `permissions.http` of
  `scene.json`, exactly (`permission_denied`). Cookies, `host` and the other
  connection headers cannot be set (`permission_denied`); at most 16 headers.
- A request body is at most 64 KB and a response at most 256 KB
  (`too_large`); each request has 15 seconds in all (`timeout`); at most 30 requests
  a minute per scene (`rate_limited`). Redirects are not followed.
- Other errors: `dns`, `connect`, `tls`, `other`, `deferred_queue_full`,
  `deferred_timeout` (see below), `not_serializable` and `too_deep` (a body table
  that cannot be sent as JSON). Errors always arrive through `cb`; only arguments
  of the wrong type are a Lua error at the call.

## scene.json

Every scene package has a `scene.json` at its root:

```json
{"id": "pomodoro", "name": "番茄钟", "version": "1.0.0", "schema_version": 1,
 "background": true, "files": "auto",
 "permissions": {"http": ["api.example.com"]}}
```

Required: `id`, `name`, `version` and `schema_version`; without any of them the
install is refused.

- `id`: 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`; also the scene's directory.
- `name`: 1 to 32 bytes of UTF-8. `version`: a semantic version, at most 64 bytes.
- `entry` (default `main.lua`) and `icon` (a file under `assets/`) are optional.
- `schema_version`: an integer from 1 to 1000, the version of the structure of the
  scene's data (see `scene.migrate` below).
- `permissions.http`: the hosts `wisp.http` may reach, at most 16.
- `background` (default `false`): going back sends the scene to the background
  instead of closing it (see Background scenes).
- `files` (default `"auto"`): where `wisp.files` keeps the scene's files: `"auto"`,
  `"sd"` or `"int"` (see wisp.files). Any other value refuses the install.

Unknown fields are ignored; nothing may nest deeper than 4 levels.

## Scene hooks

A scene sets these functions in the global `scene` table; each one that is set runs
as a message of its own, within the usual 200 ms:

- `scene.on_show()` and `scene.on_hide()`: the scene's view appears or goes (it opens,
  the screen turns on or off, it comes back from or goes to the background).
- `scene.on_close()`: the scene is closing; its store is flushed after it.
- `scene.on_state(state)`: the scene is now `"foreground"` or `"background"`. It
  is called when the scene first opens (with the state it opened in) and on every
  move between the two, never on a close.
- `scene.on_notification(id)`: the user tapped the scene's notification `id`. It is
  called once the scene is in front: one in the background comes forward first, and
  one that is not running is opened first (`wisp.scene.launch()` is then
  `"notification"`).
- `scene.migrate(old_version)`: see Data migration; it may run for 2000 ms.

## wisp.scene

- `wisp.scene.close()`: goes back, like the back gesture: a scene that declares
  `background` goes to the background, any other closes. Opening another scene does
  the same to the scene in front.
- `wisp.scene.exit()`: always closes the scene completely (`on_hide`, `on_close`).
- `wisp.scene.args()`: the table of arguments the scene was opened with (`{}` for
  none).
- `wisp.scene.state()`: `"foreground"` or `"background"`.
- `wisp.scene.launch()`: why the scene was started: `"user"`, `"boot"` (restored
  in the background after a restart) or `"notification"`.

## Background scenes

A scene whose `scene.json` declares `"background": true` keeps running after the
user goes back or opens another scene: `scene.on_hide()`, then its view goes and
`scene.on_state("background")` runs. Its VM, store, timers and widget tree
stay; changes to its state still update the tree, which is shown again when the
scene comes back to the front (from the scene list, a row of the pull-down panel or
a tap on one of its notifications), and then `scene.on_show()` and
`scene.on_state("foreground")` run. Closing it from the panel (its ×), from the
admin page or with `wisp.scene.exit()` stops it completely.

- Timers and `wisp.device.on` events keep firing in the background and while the
  screen is off, without pausing and without catching up. `wisp.http`, `wisp.store`,
  `wisp.files`, `wisp.notify`, `wisp.log` and `wisp.device.info()` work as in front.
- `wisp.sensor.subscribe`, `wisp.sensor.on` and `wisp.power.keep_screen_on` return
  `nil, "not_in_background"`; sensor subscriptions made in front pause in the
  background and resume in front. The keyboard and confirmation dialogs are not
  available. A scene in the background holds no wake lock.
- At most 3 scenes run in the background. All scenes' Lua memory comes from one
  budget of 3 MB; each scene may still use at most 2 MB, and the scene in front can always
  get its 2 MB. When a scene would go past the count, or the scene in front needs
  the memory, the scene in the background longest away from the front is closed
  (`on_close` runs and its data is saved) and the user gets a notification saying
  so.
- Scenes running in the background when the device powers off or restarts are
  started again in the background once it has booted: the entry file runs and the
  tree is built, with no view and no `on_show`; `wisp.scene.launch()` is `"boot"`.
- An error in the background stops the scene (no error panel) and posts a system
  notification.

## wisp.notify

```lua
local id = wisp.notify{ title = "番茄钟", body = "25 分钟到了",
                        sound = "alarm", wake = true, id = "pomo" }
wisp.notify_cancel(id)
```

- `title`: 1 to 32 bytes; `body`: 0 to 200 bytes (optional).
- `sound`: `"none"` (default), `"tone"` (one short tone) or `"alarm"` (rings until
  the screen is touched, at most 30 seconds). The volume is the system's
  notification volume.
- `wake` (default `false`): turns the screen on if it is off.
- `id`: optional, 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`. Posting the same id again
  replaces the earlier notification.

`wisp.notify` returns the notification's id (the one given, or one made up), or
`nil` and a code: `rate_limited` (more than 10 posts by the scene in any minute) or
`unavailable`. A bad field is a Lua error at the call. `wisp.notify_cancel(id)` removes the
scene's unread notification `id` and returns whether there was one.

A notification from a scene in the background shows a banner for 4 seconds and stays in
the pull-down panel's list until the user taps or dismisses it; each scene keeps at
most 5 unread, the oldest dropped first. A notification posted by the scene in front only
shows the banner. A tap on either calls `scene.on_notification(id)` (see Scene
hooks).

## wisp.power

- `wisp.power.keep_screen_on(on)`: `true` keeps the screen on and bright while the
  scene is in front (a `screen` wake lock), `false` lets it dim and turn off again.
  Returns `true`, or `nil` and `not_in_background` or `unavailable`. The lock goes
  by itself when the scene leaves the front or closes, and a short press of the
  power key still turns the screen off regardless. It brings no reminder: the
  scene is in front, so the user can already see the lock.

## wisp.sensor

For the scene in front only.

```lua
local h = wisp.sensor.subscribe("accel", { rate = 25 }, function(samples)
  -- samples = { {x =, y =, z =, t =}, ... }
end)
h:stop()
local g = wisp.sensor.on("shake", function() end)  -- or "flip"; g:stop()
wisp.sensor.available()                             -- { accel = true, gyro = true }
```

- `wisp.sensor.subscribe(kind, opts, fn)`: `kind` is `"accel"` or `"gyro"`;
  `opts.rate` is one of 10, 25, 50 or 100 samples a second (default 25; `opts` may be left out).
  `fn(samples)` gets the samples about every 100 ms, in a batch: `x`, `y`, `z` in
  m/s² (`accel`) or degrees per second (`gyro`), `t` in milliseconds.
- `wisp.sensor.on(gesture, fn)`: `fn()` runs on each `"shake"` (three strong jolts
  within half a second) or `"flip"` (turned face down or face up, then still for
  300 ms).
- Both return a handle, or `nil` and a code: `not_in_background`, `unavailable` (no
  such sensor) or another error's name. `h:stop()` ends it and returns whether it
  was still running.
- `wisp.sensor.available()` lists the sensors there are; `{}` without an IMU.
- Subscriptions pause while the screen is off and in the background, resume in
  front, and end when the scene closes.

## wisp.files

Each scene has its own flat directory of files, for data too large for `wisp.store`
(downloads, recordings, logs). Every call is asynchronous: `cb(err, ...)` runs
later as a message of its own, with `err` `nil` on success.

```lua
wisp.files.write(name, data, cb)          -- replaces the file; cb(err, true)
wisp.files.append(name, data, cb)         -- cb(err, true)
wisp.files.read(name, offset, len, cb)    -- cb(err, data)
wisp.files.list(cb)                       -- cb(err, { {name =, size =, mtime =}, ... }, truncated)
wisp.files.remove(name, cb)               -- cb(err, true)
wisp.files.info(cb)                       -- cb(err, { location =, want =, quota =, used = })
```

- Names: 1 to 64 bytes of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`, not starting with `.`
  and not ending in `.tmp` or `.new`; no directories. Anything else is `bad_name`.
- One `write` or `append` takes at most 256 KB and one `read` at most 64 KB
  (`too_large`); write more with several `append`s or `wisp.http.download`. `write`
  replaces the file whole or not at all.
- `list` gives at most 256 names, in name order; `truncated` is `true` when there were
  more.
- Where the files live is chosen at the scene's first write, from `files` in
  `scene.json`: `"auto"` takes the SD card when one is in and internal storage
  otherwise; `"sd"` only the SD card; `"int"` always internal storage. On the card
  a scene may use 64 MB, in internal storage 512 KB (`quota_exceeded`, and nothing
  is written). The choice is kept: a later change of `files` moves nothing.
- `files: "sd"` with no card in means the files are unavailable: every call returns
  `unavailable`, and nothing falls back to internal storage. The same goes for files
  already on a card that has been taken out; they come back with the card.
- `info` tells `location` (`"sd"` or `"int"`; absent before the first write),
  `want` (the `files` declaration), `quota` and `used` in bytes.
- The system never deletes a scene's files by itself. They go only when the user
  deletes the scene and confirms deleting its data with it, when the scene calls
  `wisp.files.remove`, or when the user deletes one on the admin page. A scene
  reinstalled with the same id finds its old files where it left them.
- Other codes: `not_found` (no such file), `unavailable`, `busy` (the storage worker
  has too much queued: try again later), `no_memory`, or the name of a storage
  error.

## wisp.http.download and deep standby

- `wisp.http.download(url, name, opts, cb)` GETs `url` (a host from
  `permissions.http`, as for `wisp.http.get`; `opts` as for `get`, may be left out)
  straight into the scene's file `name`, which it replaces once the whole body has
  arrived. It is not limited to the 256 KB of a normal response, only by the
  scene's quota. `cb(err, res)`: `res = {status, size, deferred}`. A response that
  is not 2xx leaves the file as it was and gives `size = 0`. Errors are those of
  `wisp.http` and of `wisp.files`.
- In deep standby (the screen has been off for a while) Wi-Fi is off. Requests and
  downloads then wait in a queue, at most 4 per scene (`deferred_queue_full` past
  it), until the system turns Wi-Fi on for a short network window, at most every 15
  minutes. A request that waited gets `res.deferred = true`; one that waited more
  than an hour fails with `deferred_timeout`.

## Data migration

Raise `schema_version` in `scene.json` when the structure of the scene's data
changes. When a scene opens (or is restored at boot) and its data is from a lower
version, `scene.migrate(old_version)` runs after the entry file and before the
widget tree is built, for at most 2000 ms. What the entry file and the migration write
to `wisp.store` is held back and saved, with the new version, only when the
migration returns; an error or a timeout drops all of it, leaves the data as it
was and puts the scene in error with `migrate failed: <message>`. A scene with no
`scene.migrate` just has its version raised. Data from a higher version than the
scene's (an older scene installed over a newer one) is refused: the scene does not
open.
